title: Beyond Satisfaction: Learning Associations Between Content, Reviews, and Well-Being
abstract: arXiv:2607.02539v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Recommendation algorithms shape what people consume online, yet they are primarily optimized for star ratings, likes, and sentiment, signals of user satisfaction. Whether these signals capture what is good for users, beyond momentary preference, remains largely unexamined. Well-being offers an alternative target grounded in psychology that extends beyond satisfaction. We operationalize it as immediate and enduring expressions of the five PERMA facets in reviews. Empirically, immediate positive emotion and engagement cluster as more hedonic (pleasure-oriented), while relationships, meaning, accomplishment, and enduring positive emotion and engagement behave as more eudaimonic (meaning- and growth-oriented). Analyzing 13.7 million Goodreads reviews and the content of 16 thousand books, we study how PERMA expressions differ from satisfaction targets and which book content features are associated with them. translated_title: 超越满意度：学习内容、评论与幸福感之间的关联
translated_abstract: 推荐算法塑造了人们在线消费的内容，但它们主要针对星级评分、点赞和情感等用户满意度信号进行优化。这些信号是否能捕捉到超越即时偏好的、真正对用户有益的东西，在很大程度上尚未得到研究。幸福感提供了一个植根于心理学的替代目标，超越了满意度这一范畴。我们将其操作化为评论中五个PERMA维度的即时和持久表达。实证分析表明，即时积极情绪和投入更多呈现享乐型特征（快乐导向），而人际关系、意义、成就以及持久的积极情绪和投入则表现为实现型特征（意义与成长导向）。通过分析1370万条Goodreads评论和1.6万本书的内容，我们研究了PERMA表达与满意度目标之间的差异，以及哪些书籍内容特征与它们相关联。首先，满意度信号……
tldr: 该论文提出以心理学PERMA幸福感框架替代传统满意度指标作为推荐目标，通过分析1370万条Goodreads评论和1.6万本书的内容，揭示了书籍内容特征与用户享乐型及实现型幸福感表达之间的关联。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes the psychological PERMA well-being framework as an alternative to satisfaction metrics for recommendations, analyzing 13.7 million Goodreads reviews and 16 thousand books' content to uncover associations between book content features and users' hedonic and eudaimonic well-being expressions.
